source.title: Mixture of Chapters: Scaling Learnt Memory in Transformers
source.authors: Tasmay Pankaj Tibrewal; Pritish Saha; Ankit Meda; Kunal Singh; Pradeep Moturi

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses scaling and compares a memory-augmented model with dense baselines at matched compute, but it does not test a power-law scaling relation, extrapolation, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports single-run validation-loss comparisons, not a sweep over parameter count, tokens, or compute. Those loss measurements are recorded as findings about the claim's subject, but they cannot test any listed scaling-law version. The downstream benchmark and forgetting results do not establish downstream predictability from scale or pretraining loss. The IFT loss curves compare bank-update settings, not scaling curves.
record.test_reason: The paper compares a memory-augmented transformer with two dense baselines in single 9.6B-token runs at one scale. It fits no power law, sweeps no size, data or compute, makes no extrapolation and no allocation analysis. It mentions scaling only as motivation and future work, so it tests no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors report lower pretraining loss than compute-matched dense baselines and less forgetting under IFT. They call learned memory a complementary scaling axis and leave scaling-law study of memory to future work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses a learned latent-token memory bank with chapter routing and compares models in an iso-FLOP setting; it does not fit the original studies' scaling laws or compute-optimal allocation curves.

fits_no_version.finding: At one compute budget (about 9.6B tokens), MoC reaches validation loss 2.79, versus 2.86 for the compute-matched dense model and 2.92 for the backbone-only model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this run, adding a routed learned memory bank lowers pretraining loss at matched training FLOPs.

fits_no_version.finding: After IFT, MoC has higher loss on the pretraining distribution (3.2024 vs 3.0574) but forgets less on ARC-C and BoolQ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this run, the memory-augmented model retains more benchmark knowledge through IFT despite higher pretraining-distribution loss.

record.problems: The scaling-law-relevant evidence is limited to single-run endpoint comparisons; there is no sweep, fit, or uncertainty estimate for those loss comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for the MMLU, ARC-Challenge, BoolQ, and OpenBookQA outcomes: they report benchmark comparisons and forgetting, not a scale- or pretraining-loss predictability relationship. No numerical IFT bank-update loss values are stated; the paper describes the curves as overlapping closely.

untested.parts: No sweep over parameters, tokens or compute, and no power-law fit.
No small-run fit used to predict larger runs.
No iso-FLOP sweep of parameter/token splits. The 'iso-FLOP' baseline is a single matched model.
No fixed-parameter comparison of depth or width.
No scaling curve in another modality or regime. IFT is reported only at one scale.
Benchmarks are reported for three models at roughly one scale. No relation to scale or loss is tested.
No fitted exponents and no comparison of fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The 'new axis of scaling' claim rests on one compute point. The paper also notes that freezing the bank during IFT performs on par with updating it. None of this bears on V1–V7.

versions.untested_parts: No multi-scale sweep or fitted power law in parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fit or prediction of substantially larger runs.
No sweep over parameter/token allocations at fixed compute and no compute-optimal allocation fit.
No architecture comparison holding parameter count fixed to test effects of depth, width, or other details.
No scaling-law test in another modality or training regime.
Benchmarks are reported for model variants, but no predictable relationship between downstream performance and scale or pretraining loss is tested.
No comparison of fitted exponents, fitting choices, or departures from a single power law.
